subject: chemistry
title: Entropy
key_idea: **Entropy**, S, measures how dispersed the energy and particles in a system are: the more ways they can be arranged, the higher the entropy. Change goes in the direction of increasing total entropy. This is why some endothermic reactions happen.

blocks.text: Enthalpy alone cannot explain why reactions happen. Some endothermic reactions go ahead at room temperature, so another factor must be involved.

items.meaning: A measure of the dispersal of energy in a system. It is greater the more disordered the system, and the more ways the particles and their energy can be arranged.
The final entropy minus the initial entropy. It is positive when the system becomes more disordered.
The entropy of 1 mol of a substance under standard conditions. Its units are J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

items: Energy and matter tend to spread out. A hot object cools by spreading energy to its surroundings, and a gas expands to fill its container.
The natural direction of change is towards an increase in the total entropy of the system and its surroundings.
Entropy values are never negative. A perfect crystal at 0 K has zero entropy.
Entropy changes are small, so they are measured in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, not kJ.
Entropy measures the dispersal of energy and particles.
Total entropy tends to increase, so ΔS(total) is positive for a change that happens.
Units of entropy are J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.

blocks.text: You can predict whether ΔS for a system is positive or negative by asking whether the particles end up with more freedom.

rows: Particles move more freely, so there are more arrangements
Particles have more energy, spread over more energy levels
The ordered lattice breaks up and ions disperse in solution
More moles of gas on the right
Gases have far greater entropy than solids and liquids
Fewer moles of gas on the right
The gas molecules are fewer and more ordered

items: Order of entropy for a substance: solid < liquid << gas. The step from liquid to gas is the largest.
For a reaction, count the moles of gas on each side. A change in gas moles has a bigger effect than any other.
Some dissolving is the exception: ions with a high charge density order the water molecules around them, which can make ΔS negative.

items: Gases have much higher entropy than liquids and solids.
More moles of gas gives a positive ΔS; fewer gives a negative ΔS.
Melting, boiling, dissolving and heating usually raise entropy.

blocks.text: Use standard entropy values to find ΔS for the system. Then use the enthalpy change to find ΔS for the surroundings. The two add up to the total.

blocks.label: Entropy change of the system
where: Σ = sum of (moles × standard entropy) for each substance

diagram.alt: Practise calculating the entropy change of the system for the formation of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen.
diagram.question: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g). S⦵ values: N₂ **{n}**, H₂ **{h}**, NH₃ **{a}** J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. Calculate ΔS(system).
working: ΔS(system) = products − reactants = **{answer}** J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (negative: 4 mol of gas becomes 2 mol)

blocks.label: Entropy change of the surroundings
where: ΔH = enthalpy change of the reaction, in J mol⁻¹ (multiply kJ by 1000)

blocks.label: Total entropy change
where: all terms in J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹

items: An exothermic reaction releases heat. This disperses energy into the surroundings, so ΔS(surroundings) is positive.
An endothermic reaction takes heat in, so ΔS(surroundings) is negative.
A reaction can happen if ΔS(total) is positive, even if ΔS(system) is negative.
An endothermic reaction can happen when ΔS(system) is positive and large enough to make ΔS(total) positive.
ΔS(system) = Σproducts − Σreactants.
ΔS(surroundings) = −ΔH ÷ T, with ΔH converted to J.
The reaction happens when ΔS(total) is positive.

checks.q: Predict the sign of ΔS for 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g). Explain your answer.
checks.a: Positive. A gas is produced from liquids, and gases have much higher entropy because their particles can be arranged in many more ways.

checks.q: A reaction has ΔH = −92 kJ mol⁻¹ at 298 K. Calculate ΔS(surroundings).
Explain how an endothermic reaction can occur at room temperature.
checks.a: ΔS(surroundings) is negative, but if ΔS(system) is positive and larger in size, ΔS(total) is positive, so the reaction is favoured.

items: Explain why entropy differs between solids, liquids and gases.
Explain the effect of a change in the number of gaseous molecules in a reaction on the entropy.
Calculate ΔS for a reaction from the entropies of the reactants and products.

Discuss typical reactions in terms of disorder and enthalpy change: dissolving ammonium nitrate crystals in water, ethanoic acid with ammonium carbonate, burning magnesium ribbon in air, and solid barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)₂·8H₂O) with solid ammonium chloride.

The first, second and fourth are endothermic and still go ahead: ΔS(system) is positive and large, because a solid becomes liquid or gas. Burning magnesium is exothermic: it releases so much heat that ΔS(surroundings) is large and positive, even though ΔS(system) is negative.
Define entropy as the number of possible arrangements of the particles and their energy in a given system.
Predict and explain the sign of ΔS for a change of state, a temperature change, and a reaction that changes the number of gaseous molecules.
ΔS⦵ = ΣS⦵(products) − ΣS⦵(reactants). Using ΔS(total) = ΔS(surroundings) + ΔS(system) is not required.
